The Lord looks past the stumblings of the soul.

Honest, reaching, longing to be whole.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The first breath, and the last amen.
For the Spirit speaks within.
So pour your whole heart out.
A constant prayer for everything I feel.
To come with real intent and not with pride.
And lay them down with nothing left to hide.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,

Just talk to Him — and then
Be still, and learn to listen,
For the Spirit speaks within.

In the name of Jesus Christ,

sheet: I don't have pretty words or practiced speech,
No memorized petition, polished bright.
Just everything that's tangled in my heart—
The gratitude, the worry, and the fight.
He told me God don't care about the language,
The Lord looks past the stumblings of the soul.
So I speak the way a child speaks to a Father—
Honest, reaching, longing to be whole.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The first breath, and the last amen.
On bended knees or striving through the dark,
Just talk to Him — and then
Be still, and learn to listen,
For the Spirit speaks within.
The Father hears you, every word—
So pour your whole heart out.
Sometimes I bow my head before the sunrise.
Sometimes I cry for help with no time to kneel.
Sometimes it's just a whisper while I'm working—
A constant prayer for everything I feel.

To come with real intent and not with pride.

And lay them down with nothing left to hide.

The first breath, and the last amen.

For the Spirit speaks within.

So pour your whole heart out.

But then I paused — and something stirred inside me,
A still, small voice I'd never learned to heed.
He speaks to mind and heart at once,
A burning and a peace.
The Spirit carries back His word
Until the questions cease.
This is how the Father answers—
Not in thunder, but in light.
He said, "Ask, and I will show you."
And He meant it. And He's right.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The offering that never ends.
He knew my needs before I spoke—
And still He calls me friend.
So speak, and then be still and listen,
For the heavens aren't sealed tight.
The God who spoke to prophets old
Still speaks from the light.

Think things over, and then ask God.
He'll cause your heart to burn
if it's right and true.
He's the same God He's always been.
And He is waiting for you now…
when you're ready.
In the name of Jesus Christ,
Amen.

sheet: How long have we sought the Eternal Father,
who created us to seek Him?
How long through silence, shadow, and the dark?
We have carried His name —
but have we known His heart?
In one voice, in one mind —
we come home to Him.
God is not a fable told against the silence —
He was moved by love to give us life.
He weeps when His children go astray.
More present than doubt, more enduring than distance —
the God who feels is the God who remains faithful.
He sent us His Son — no shadow, no pretense —
Christ wore our flesh and was sore amazed,
as He knelt in the garden’s dark to know us.
His living mission: to gather us with Him.
This we hold with one voice and one mind:
He is real. He is near. He has not left us behind.
Through the shadows and doubt, in the light and the clear —
one faith, one hope — we hold each other here.
His grace is not a transaction — it is His power.
It enters the cracks and rebuilds us from within.
We are not left where His grace first found us —
we are formed by the grace we were made for.
He calls us to ripeness, to wholeness, to flourishing —
His image growing in us day by day.
Not crushed by impossible standards,
but gently becoming beneath His steady gaze.
He said life eternal begins now, not later —
to know the living God is where it starts.
We do not have to wait for what He promised —
the Kingdom is at hand for willing hearts.
The vessels who bore His word were cracked —
earthen jars, just as we are.
Yet the water runs pure though the vessel is clay,
and the wellspring has never run dry.
He sets His table for all of His children;
He denies none who come — not a single one.
All are alike unto God in this gathering —
the lost and the seeking, the weak and the strong.
He builds up the Church of the Lamb,
gathering us from every nation and shore.
No gatekeepers stand at the door He has opened —
all who are His He has called, and will shelter.
By this the world will know we belong to Him —
not by doctrine, traditions, or names,
but by love that carries the weight of another,
that mourns with the mourning and shoulders the shame.
And that —
they all —
may be —
ONE —
As the Father and Son.
Not one in opinion — but one in His love,
that never abandons and burns bright always.
We see through a glass, and we see only in part.
Our knowing is dim, but our knowing is real.
Our holding is honest. We hold as we are able,
and we walk by His light that lives in our heart.
And when there is nothing but stubborn hope left —
when faith is a wrestle, but our grip will not weaken —
we cling to His covenant — anyway — always —
for He gathers His own, even when our strength gives way.
This we hold with one voice and one mind:
He is real. He is near. He has not left us behind.
Through the shadows and doubt, in the light and the clear —
one faith, one hope — we hold each other here.
That they may all be one — as the Father and Son —
this is the prayer that gathers us in one.
We hold on. He holds more. We press on. He goes before.
In one voice — He is real.
In one mind — He is near.
He has not left us behind.
In one voice, in one mind — we come home to Him.

rows.title: Keep Me Turning to You
rows.label: Cinematic Orchestra

unsung.text: Savior, help me turn to what is warm and true.
I never could climb alone to Heaven;
this broken soul was never mine to mend.
So Jesus, keep me turning to You,
walking the path that leads me home.
Grace was never wages waiting
at the ending of the fight;
grace is strength inside the struggle,
grace is power for the climb.
Line upon line You remake me —
You are not done with me yet —
not a Judge who counts my failures,
but a Father who forgives.
And the sins I laid before You,
You remember them no more,
till I stand within Your glory,
unashamed before the Lord.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart belongs to You.

sheet: I used to wait for the breaking point,
the edge of shame and desperation,
before I could lift my voice to You,
falling into Your healing arms.
But Your mercy outlasts dark nights —
it knocks at my door each morning.
Now I know, turning to You isn't weakness;
it isn't crawling back in shame.
I stand tallest on my knees in prayer.
Worldly sorrow heals no wounds,
it's just a cell that locks me in;
it never once has made me clean —
it only names my grief and sins.
But the sorrow that comes from Heaven
is a door thrown open wide;
it does not leave me in despair —

grace is strength inside the struggle,
grace is power for the climb.

sheet: I was a traveler, lost among the hills,
Until the Shepherd's voice found me still.
I stand a witness of the risen, living Christ—
Whose mercy held me fast, whose love has paid my price.
We are all of us so human,
Travelers wrapped in dust and skin,
Searching for a clearing where the light comes pouring in.
Our untamed hearts keep pulling toward the wild and the unknown,
We wrestle through the bitter and the sweet to find our way back home,
Walking through the shadow and the beauty, never quite alone.
For we are hunters! We are gatherers of light,
Reaching for the sacred in the middle of the night.
Not with the wisdom of the world or the scholars' heavy pen,
But in the language of a father—where the plainness all begins.
Speaking truth to searching souls, to harmonize and heal—
In the words of plainness, He makes the broken whole,
In the words of plainness, He's calling to your soul.
These are letters for the unborn, a heritage of grace,
For the ones who'll walk this wide and weary place.
Because He first came looking, we will never walk alone—
My soul delights in plainness—
Not the gilded words of men,
But the simple truth that finds us
And brings us home again.
For we are hunters! We are gatherers of light,
Reaching for the sacred in the middle of the night—
In the words of plainness, He's calling to your soul.
These words of mine are plain, but oh, my heart is full.
I am a debtor to His grace, a receiver of His mercy.
Jesus is the Christ—the Light that finds us in the dark.
In Him I find my rest.
In His holy name, amen.

rows.title: Two Halves of a Whole
rows.label: Celtic Ballad

runs.heard: all my knowing, looking out across

sheet: I've walked the avenues of life,
I've tasted rain and summer's heat.
I've gathered pearls of wisdom, simply beautiful,
And laid them down here at the Teacher's feet.
The world is organized in such complexity,
The Architect is found in every stone.
But even when survival needs are met,
A hunger stays for something still unknown.
For truth is knowledge as things really are,
A light that shines on what is yet to come.
Science isn't blind and faith isn't lame
When we see them both as one.
It's a fuller way of walking on the road
Where every path to truth is joined together.
We're chasing down the meaning of our days,
By the love of God directed, now and ever.
I've built my intellectual altars to the mind
Through philosophy and arts and the sciences.
I've analyzed the patterns and the laws
And let my thinking be my sole reliance.
But academic means can only go so far,
They're limited by things we can't perceive.
We're ever learning, never coming to the truth
Without the courage to truly believe.
Now I'm standing at the ceiling of the framework,
Looking through the window at the rain.
Reason is a shadow in the moonlight
If it cannot take away the pain.
Why is there something rather than nothing at all?
Does who I am persist beyond the grave?
I'm reaching for the eyes that have been hidden,
For the spirit that the Savior came to save.
I choose to experiment upon the word.
I choose the foresight of the prophecy.
The spirit speaks what senses never heard—
It's the power of God that sets the seeker free!
So I'll walk in wondering humility,
Recognizing that I know so very little.
The world may shift like shadows on the wall,
But a simple truth is resting in the middle.
Great ignorance might lead a man to fear,
And knowledge brings a measure of our sorrow.
But wisdom brings a peace that's resting here
And a hope for every bright tomorrow.
Life has grand purpose.
A beautiful and simple way.
In the name of Jesus Christ,
Amen.

rows.title: The Marks of Your Worth
rows.label: Ministry Anthem
sheet: Come, O Source of endless mercy,
Loose my tongue to sing Thy grace.
Streams of goodness, ever flowing,
Fill the hollows in this soul of mine.
I have tasted bitter waters,
Trying to satisfy the thirst.
But the Shepherd’s voice spoke clearly—
Called this wandering stranger home.
Come to Me, all worn and weary.
Look to Me, and live.
Learn of Me — My grace sustains you.
Can you hear Me… calling your name?
Now I speak in words of plainness:
With Thy help this far I’ve come.
I hope by Thy tender mercy
Safely to return back home.
Far from Thee and full of questions,
I knelt down and poured out my soul.
He healed every empty place in me,
Made my broken vessel whole.
My arms are open.
My wounded heart still beats for you.
My hands will bless you.
The marks of your worth remain on Me.
By Thy goodness, I was found.
Now I bear a joyful debt to carry!
To Thy grace I am now bound.
Turn now my wandering heart to Thee:
Prone to wander, Lord, I feel it,
Prone to leave the path You’ve shown;
Here’s my soul — O take and seal it,
Bring me to my heavenly home.
Take My name upon you.
The marks of your worth remain on Me.
You are no stranger now—
I call you by name.
Bring my heavenly home to me,
And bring me to my heavenly home.

rows.title: One Voice, One Mind
rows.label: Interfaith Anthem
sheet: How long have we sought the Eternal Father,
who created us to seek Him?
How long through silence, shadow, and the dark?
We have carried His name —
but have we known His heart?
In one voice, in one mind —
we come home to Him.
God is not a fable told against the silence —
He was moved by love to give us life.
He weeps when His children go astray.
More present than doubt, more enduring than distance —
the God who feels is the God who remains faithful.
He sent us His Son — no shadow, no pretense —
Christ wore our flesh and was sore amazed,
as He knelt in the garden’s dark to know us.
His living mission: to gather us with Him.
This we hold with one voice and one mind:
He is real. He is near. He has not left us behind.
Through the shadows and doubt, in the light and the clear —
one faith, one hope — we hold each other here.
His grace is not a transaction — it is His power.
It enters the cracks and rebuilds us from within.
We are not left where His grace first found us —
we are formed by the grace we were made for.
He calls us to ripeness, to wholeness, to flourishing —
His image growing in us day by day.
Not crushed by impossible standards,
but gently becoming beneath His steady gaze.
He said life eternal begins now, not later —
to know the living God is where it starts.
We do not have to wait for what He promised —
the Kingdom is at hand for willing hearts.
The vessels who bore His word were cracked —
earthen jars, just as we are.
Yet the water runs pure though the vessel is clay,
and the wellspring has never run dry.
He sets His table for all of His children;
He denies none who come — not a single one.
All are alike unto God in this gathering —
the lost and the seeking, the weak and the strong.
He builds up the Church of the Lamb,
gathering us from every nation and shore.
No gatekeepers stand at the door He has opened —
all who are His He has called, and will shelter.
By this the world will know we belong to Him —
not by doctrine, traditions, or names,
but by love that carries the weight of another,
that mourns with the mourning and shoulders the shame.
And that —
they all —
may be —
ONE —
As the Father and Son.
Not one in opinion — but one in His love,
that never abandons and burns bright always.
We see through a glass, and we see only in part.
Our knowing is dim, but our knowing is real.
Our holding is honest. We hold as we are able,
and we walk by His light that lives in our heart.
And when there is nothing but stubborn hope left —
when faith is a wrestle, but our grip will not weaken —
we cling to His covenant — anyway — always —
for He gathers His own, even when our strength gives way.
This we hold with one voice and one mind:
He is real. He is near. He has not left us behind.
Through the shadows and doubt, in the light and the clear —
one faith, one hope — we hold each other here.
That they may all be one — as the Father and Son —
this is the prayer that gathers us in one.
We hold on. He holds more. We press on. He goes before.
In one voice — He is real.
In one mind — He is near.
He has not left us behind.
In one voice, in one mind — we come home to Him.

rows.title: Introduction to Plainness
rows.label: Sacred Americana
sheet: I was a traveler, lost among the hills,
Until the Shepherd's voice found me still.
I stand a witness of the risen, living Christ—
Whose mercy held me fast, whose love has paid my price.
We are all of us so human,
Travelers wrapped in dust and skin,
Searching for a clearing where the light comes pouring in.
Our untamed hearts keep pulling toward the wild and the unknown,
We wrestle through the bitter and the sweet to find our way back home,
Walking through the shadow and the beauty, never quite alone.
For we are hunters! We are gatherers of light,
Reaching for the sacred in the middle of the night.
Not with the wisdom of the world or the scholars' heavy pen,
But in the language of a father—where the plainness all begins.
Speaking truth to searching souls, to harmonize and heal—
In the words of plainness, He makes the broken whole,
In the words of plainness, He's calling to your soul.
These are letters for the unborn, a heritage of grace,
For the ones who'll walk this wide and weary place.
Because He first came looking, we will never walk alone—
My soul delights in plainness—
Not the gilded words of men,
But the simple truth that finds us
And brings us home again.
For we are hunters! We are gatherers of light,
Reaching for the sacred in the middle of the night—
In the words of plainness, He's calling to your soul.
These words of mine are plain, but oh, my heart is full.
I am a debtor to His grace, a receiver of His mercy.
Jesus is the Christ—the Light that finds us in the dark.
In Him I find my rest.
In His holy name, amen.

rows.title: Our Search
rows.label: Sacred Americana
sheet: There's a hunger deep inside I cannot name
Feelin' homesick for a place I've never known
Filled it up with pride and empty pleasure
Oh, but bitter waters never satisfy
I've walked roads of despair and rebellion
Let go of who I was to fit a mold
Made excuses out of worldly wisdom
But clever words can't warm a weary soul
Seek and you will find
Knock and the door swings open wide
There's a humble road between the shadows
Where the hungry come to find the light
The search is worth the risking
Every question, every climb
Seek and you will find
I see it now through a glass so darkly
But even shadows cannot hide what's true
There's meaning waiting just past my understanding
A living water, crystal, still, and free
Reflecting back the face of God in me
Seek and you will find
Knock and the door swings open wide
There's a humble road between the shadows
Where the hungry come to find the light
The search is worth the risking
Every question, every climb
Seek and you will find
Between the pride and the despair
Between the running and standing still
There's a narrow way for honest seekers
Where the deepest thirst is finally filled
Seek and you will find
Knock and the door swings open wide
There's a humble road between the shadows
Where the hungry come to find the light
The search is worth the risking
Worth any sacrifice
Seek and you will find
Seek and you will find
Seek and you will find
The hunger was no curse
God planted it on purpose
A holy homesickness
To lead me home

rows.title: Two Halves of a Whole
rows.label: Americana Folk
sheet: I've walked the avenues of life,
I've tasted rain and summer's heat.
I've gathered pearls of wisdom, simply beautiful,
And laid them down here at the Teacher's feet.
The world is organized in such complexity,
The Architect is found in every stone.
But even when survival needs are met,
A hunger stays for something still unknown.
For truth is knowledge as things really are,
A light that shines on what is yet to come.
Science isn't blind and faith isn't lame
When we see them both as one.
It's a fuller way of walking on the road
Where every path to truth is joined together.
We're chasing down the meaning of our days,
By the love of God directed, now and ever.
I've built my intellectual altars to the mind
Through philosophy and arts and the sciences.
I've analyzed the patterns and the laws
And let my thinking be my sole reliance.
But academic means can only go so far,
They're limited by things we can't perceive.
We're ever learning, never coming to the truth
Without the courage to truly believe.
Now I'm standing at the ceiling of the framework,
Looking through the window at the rain.
Reason is a shadow in the moonlight
If it cannot take away the pain.
Why is there something rather than nothing at all?
Does who I am persist beyond the grave?
I'm reaching for the eyes that have been hidden,
For the spirit that the Savior came to save.
I choose to experiment upon the word.
I choose the foresight of the prophecy.
The spirit speaks what senses never heard—
It's the power of God that sets the seeker free!
I'm reaching for the eyes that have been hidden,
So I'll walk in wondering humility,
Recognizing that I know so very little.
The world may shift like shadows on the wall,
But a simple truth is resting in the middle.
Great ignorance might lead a man to fear,
And knowledge brings a measure of our sorrow.
But wisdom brings a peace that's resting here
And a hope for every bright tomorrow.
Life has grand purpose.
A beautiful and simple way.
In the name of Jesus Christ,
Amen.

rows.title: When God Becomes Real
rows.label: Sacred Americana
sheet: I've chased down every question
Read the books and followed every thread
But standing at the edge of all I know
I feel a deeper hunger in me
There's a thirst that won't be satisfied
By everything the world has shown
We gather pearls of wisdom as we go
But the deepest truths remain unknown
We learn from what our senses tell us
We trust the ones who came before
We reason through the darkness for a light
But something's calling out for more
Human minds have built cathedrals
Mapped the stars and split the atom wide
But when I ask "Why am I here?"
The world has never satisfied
Ever learning, never landing
On the ground where certainty begins
I've found the limits of my reach —
Now I'm ready to look within
Faith and learning, companions in the same cause
Walking toward the light that never dims
What the mind begins to question
The spirit can complete
Truth is knowable — God is not silent
He's waiting at the edge of all we seek
How did all of this begin?
Is there purpose in the change?
Is someone guiding, watching, reaching down
To meet me where I am?
I won't cling to fear of answers
I won't hide behind my doubt
Great wisdom leads to peace, I'm told
And I'm ready to find out
Faith and learning, companions in the same cause
Walking toward the light that never dims
What the mind begins to question
The spirit can complete
Truth is knowable — God is not silent
He's waiting at the edge of all we seek
I am more than flesh and reasoning
There's a spirit living here inside
When I reached beyond what I could prove
That's when God became real to me
The questions didn't disappear
But fear gave way to hope
In the stillness something spoke to me:
"You were never searching alone"
This is when God becomes real —
Not a theory, but a voice you feel
Faith and learning, companions in the same cause
Walking toward the light that never dims
What the mind begins to question
The spirit can complete
Truth is knowable — God is not silent
He's waiting at the edge of all we seek
So if you're standing where I stood
Hungry, searching, wondering if it's real
Ask Him — just speak what's in your heart
He has answered me
He will answer you
Truth is knowable
Peace can be found
This I promise
In the name of Jesus Christ
Amen.

rows.title: The Soul's Sincere Desire
rows.label: Soul Worship
sheet: I don't have pretty words or practiced speech,
No memorized petition, polished bright.
Just everything that's tangled in my heart—
The gratitude, the worry, and the fight.
He told me God don't care about the language,
The Lord looks past the stumblings of the soul.
So I speak the way a child speaks to a Father—
Honest, reaching, longing to be whole.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The first breath, and the last amen.
On bended knees or striving through the dark,
Just talk to Him — and then
Be still, and learn to listen,
For the Spirit speaks within.
The Father hears you, every word—
So pour your whole heart out.
Sometimes I bow my head before the sunrise.
Sometimes I cry for help with no time to kneel.
Sometimes it's just a whisper while I'm working—
A constant prayer for everything I feel.
He said to pray in closets, not for show,
To come with real intent and not with pride.
So here behind the door, I bring my burdens,
And lay them down with nothing left to hide.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The first breath, and the last amen.
On bended knees or striving through the dark,
Just talk to Him — and then
Be still, and learn to listen,
For the Spirit speaks within.
The Father hears you, every word—
So pour your whole heart out.
I used to think that prayer was only asking,
Sending words like postcards, never received.
But then I paused — and something stirred inside me,
A still, small voice I'd never learned to heed.
He speaks to mind and heart at once,
A burning and a peace.
The Spirit carries back His word
Until the questions cease.
This is how the Father answers—
Not in thunder, but in light.
He said, "Ask, and I will show you."
And He meant it. And He's right.
Prayer is the soul's sincere desire,
The offering that never ends.
He knew my needs before I spoke—
And still He calls me friend.
So speak, and then be still and listen,
For the heavens aren't sealed tight.
The God who spoke to prophets old
Still speaks from the light.
Pray always… listen well.
Think things over, and then ask God.
He'll cause your heart to burn
if it's right and true.
He's the same God He's always been.
And He is waiting for you now…
when you're ready.
In the name of Jesus Christ,
Amen.

rows.title: Promises Kept
rows.label: Folk Hymn
sheet: Before the morning star was named,
before the covenant was sealed,
a lamb laid on an altar stone
and heaven began to say:
He is coming.
He is coming.
Wait on the Lord — hold on.
You have carried promises too —
through silence and through wondering years.
Those who hope and quietly wait
are not forgotten — they are carried.
Your strength will rise like eagles rising.
Rest in Him and do not strive.
You, too, Lord — keep Your word.
He is coming.
He is coming.
Wait on the Lord — we will hold on.
Mary said yes to what she could not see
and treasured all she could not understand.
Joseph said yes to what he did not know —
heaven placed in mortal hands.
He came. He came.
The night that never went dark.
She pondered these things in her heart —
and so can you.
He came. He came.
God keeping His ancient word.
Ponder these things in your heart.
You have your own unspoken years,
your own familiar bench and trade —
ordinary days of faithful living,
the hidden years inside His plan.
He grew in wisdom and in stature,
in favor with God and man.
And so do you — in ways unseen,
in every quiet, steady span.
Mary said yes to what she could not see
and treasured all she could not understand.
Joseph said yes to what he did not know —
heaven placed in mortal hands.
He came. He came.
The night that never went dark.
She pondered these things in her heart —
and so can you.
He came. He came.
God keeping His ancient word.
Ponder these things in your heart.
And when the time has come for you to leave
the workbench and the road you know,
trust in the Lord with all your heart —
lean not on what you think you see.
Acknowledge Him in all your ways
and He will make the pathway clear.
For we walk by faith and not by sight —
this is the word He speaks to you right here.
He said yes before the world began.
She said yes in a Galilean town.
And you — can say yes today,
as all His promises come down.
He came. He came.
God keeping His word through it all.
He came. He came —
and nothing faithful will be small.
Wait on the Lord.
Be of good courage.
He kept His word.
Wait on the Lord.
He will renew your strength.
He always keeps His word.

rows.title: Established in Him
rows.label: Sacred Americana
sheet: The scriptures call Him the Bridegroom,
His Church the beloved bride.
Discipleship is the wedding dance —
Come walk with me inside.
I opened Your journal and there You are —
Not the stranger I'd imagined.
A heart so tender it stuns me still,
A love too patient to measure.
The more I look, the more I behold —
Mercy woven through every word.
Something in me begins to rise,
Like a song I always knew but never heard.
Like the joy of a bride on her wedding day,
Received by her Lord at the altar —
Every heart overflowing, every voice lifted high,
We behold You, Yehoshua — established we are.
Now I see in Your eyes what You see in me —
Every broken moment, now mending.
You don't turn away from what I've been —
You call me forward into Your knowing.
My heart swells. My soul is claimed.
I am walking in Your light.
Not alone — not anymore.
Yoked together, every labor feels right.
Like the joy of a bride on her wedding day,
Received by her Lord at the altar —
Every heart overflowing, every voice lifted high,
We behold You, Yehoshua — established we are.
At the feast You have prepared, we eat and drink —
Your grace has made us more than we could be.
For most of Your holy life You worked the wood and stone,
Dust on Your hands and feet.
A household fed by labor,
Joy around the table — years among Your own.
And now I'm one of them.
A foundation laid in quiet repetition
For a glory none could yet imagine.
So I set my hands to what is mine —
The humble road now holy ground beneath me.
Each ordinary day a preparation,
Built on faithfulness and laughter.
Like the joy of a bride on her wedding day,
Received by her Lord at the altar —
Every heart overflowing, every voice lifted high,
We behold You, Yehoshua — established we are.
At the feast You have prepared, we eat and drink —
Your grace has made us more than we could be.
Entering Your mansions, every promise fulfilled —
A new life everlasting begins now with You.
Father, thank You for the heart of Your Son.
Thank You for letting me see as I have been seen —
For the table, the labor, and the road ahead.
Make me faithful in the ordinary days,
Joyful in the dust and duty,
And worthy of the name I now carry.
In His holy name, Jesus Christ, amen.

rows.title: He Always Knew Me
rows.label: Cinematic Worship
sheet: I — have worn too many names.
Tried to find the one that fits.
Identified myself by what I've done.
Cared what the world thinks.
Afraid to come up empty.
Afraid to leave no mark.
Traded everything I was.
Trying to find out who I am.
But in the garden in the dark.
He — didn't come to teach or speak.
Christ — measured the full weight of me.
Every sorrow, every dream.
Every shame I've carried quietly.
Every hope I couldn't name.
He felt it all from the inside.
And — He didn't turn away.
You always knew me.
Before I knew myself.
You didn't wait for me to find you.
You came to know me first, earn my trust.
I am a child of God.
That's who I've always been.
I don't have to search anymore.
I'm already known.
I'm already loved.
I've found my heavenly home.
He — didn't stay dead, He lives
That's the thing that makes it real.
He — rose and works among the faithful still.
Not a memory.
Not just an ideal.
All that time I spent on fear.
All that searching, all that weight.
Now I set it free — and I'll use it well.
On something worth my days.
Not just a teacher.
Not just a death.
He used the power of Creation.
To know me first.
And knowing me completely.
He thought I was worth His life.
He thought you were worth it, too.
He still does.
You always knew me.
Before I knew myself.
You didn't wait for me to find you.
You came to know me first, earn my trust.
I am a child of God, and so are you.
You don't have to search anymore.
You're already known.
You're already loved.
Welcome home...
The search is over it was always over.
He just wanted you to know.
In the name of Jesus Christ.
Amen.

rows.title: Panteles
rows.label: Sacred Ballad
sheet: They watched Him rise until the cloud received Him.
And stood there staring at an empty sky.
Two angels came and asked them gently.
Why are you looking up?
What looked like leaving was a promise kept:
I will not leave you here alone.
Two walked a road with hearts too heavy to see.
He broke the bread, and then they knew.
He ever lives — He is not gone.
Panteles — to the uttermost,
Completely, for all time, for anyone.
No gatekeeper stands at His door.
That burning is not ancient history.
It is alive in any road you walk.
A warmth of heart, a conscience growing clear.
A pull toward goodness in the dark.
The question is not was my lamp once lit?
But is it burning still today?
His grace is not just words that leave you where you are.
It is a power that can change.
He ever lives — He is not gone.
Panteles — to the uttermost,
Completely, for all time, for anyone.
No gatekeeper stands at His door.
Whatever looking back has cost you,
The plow is still in the field.
Whatever name you carry, wherever you have been,
The choice to turn is here.
He ever lives — He is not gone.
Panteles — to the uttermost,
No gatekeeper stands at His door.
He lives — come walk with Him today.
He is present.
Always, everywhere,
For everyone.
In the name of Jesus Christ.
Amen.

rows.title: What You Were Made to Be
rows.label: Acoustic Worship
sheet: I read the Bee-attitudes like a list of things I'm not—
Every line a mirror showing everything wrong inside me.
"Be ye therefore perfect" kept me striving, kept me small,
Till I learned the word means finished—not "you'd better never fall."
Blessed means flourishing—that's the word He chose.
Not "make yourself worthy," not "put on better clothes."
It's the life that's genuinely good, the life He came to give—
Not a standard you can't reach, but a way to truly live.
This is what you were made to be—
Not flawless, but completed—not fallen, but free.
The kingdom is yours. The kingdom is now.
He's finishing what He started—let me show you how.
It starts with honest seeing—poor in spirit means you're real.
You stop the performance, drop the mask, and say the things you feel.
The Lord is near the brokenhearted—that's the door that lets Him in.
And comfort isn't fixing you—it's God beside you as you grow.
You can loosen up your grip—meekness isn't being weak.
Strength governed by discipline, power restrained by wisdom.
And the hunger runs in you like a river going dry—
The soul that thirsts for righteousness will never be denied.
This is what you were made to be—
Not flawless, but completed—not fallen, but free.
The kingdom is yours. The kingdom is now.
He's finishing what He started—let me show you how.
Mercy costs you something—it always does, it always will.
It owns debts it didn't earn, love that satisfies justice.
But the pure in heart—they'll see Him.
They'll see Him.
Beholding changes everything—from glory into glory.
His image in your countenance, created in His image.

rows.title: The First One I Turn To
rows.label: A Cappella
sheet: I showed up every morning, I showed up every night
Said the words I thought You wanted, closed the book and put out the light
All those hours in between us, I was walking on my own
Leaning on my own understanding, holding my breath while all alone
Lord, teach me how to never stop talking to You
Every waking moment, turn my heart before I move
Teach me how to pray until the praying becomes joy
Until Your voice becomes my inspiration — the air I'm learning to breathe
There came a season that broke me — problems bigger than my pride
Crying out between my heartbeats, nowhere left for me to hide
"Lord, help me see this clearly" — "God, I don't know what to do"
Then something changed — not the circumstance, but who my heart turns to
Lord, show me how to never stop turning to You
Every broken moment, turn my heart before I move
Show me how to pray until the praying becomes joy
Until Your presence is my atmosphere — the only air I need
I stopped filling empty silence
And You were already there
The problem was never Your quiet —
The noise was always mine to bear
So I'm learning how to listen
Learning how to wait
I need You more than I need answers —
It's the air I'm learning to breathe
Lord, teach me how to never stop living in You
Every ordinary moment, turn my heart before I move
Teach me how to pray until the praying becomes joy
Until Your peace surrounds me and sustains me day and night
Don't let me hold my breath again
Don't let me walk this road alone
I want to live inside Your presence all my days

rows.title: Keep Me Turning to You
rows.label: Piano Ballad
sheet: I used to wait for the breaking point,
the edge of shame and desperation,
before I could lift my voice to You,
falling into Your healing arms.
But Your mercy outlasts dark nights —
it knocks at my door each morning.
Now I know, turning to You isn't weakness;
it isn't crawling back in shame.
I stand tallest on my knees in prayer.
Worldly sorrow heals no wounds,
it's just a cell that locks me in;
it never once has made me clean —
it only names my grief and sins.
But the sorrow that comes from Heaven
is a door thrown open wide;
it does not leave me in despair —
and Heaven whispers gently: come unto me.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart leans to You.
When I wander, when I'm weary, when I'm cold,
Savior, help me turn to what is warm and true.
I never could climb alone to Heaven;
this broken soul was never mine to mend.
So Jesus, keep me turning to You,
walking the path that leads me home.
There are choices I keep in shadow,
there are words I will not say,
and the weight of what I'm hiding
only grows from day to day.
So I put these things upon Your altar,
and I name them in the light —
and the things I thought would ruin me
loosed their hold on me this night.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart leans to You.
When I wander, when I'm weary, when I'm cold,
Savior, help me turn to what is warm and true.
I never could climb alone to Heaven;
this broken soul was never mine to mend.
So Jesus, keep me turning to You,
walking the path that leads me home.
Grace was never wages waiting
at the ending of the fight;
grace is strength inside the struggle,
grace is power for the climb.
Line upon line You remake me —
You are not done with me yet —
not a Judge who counts my failures,
but a Father who forgives.
And the sins I laid before You,
You remember them no more,
till I stand within Your glory,
unashamed before the Lord.
So keep me turning, Lord, morning and night —
till my whole heart belongs to You.
And when I stand within Your glory,
let me fear Your face no more —
not because I never wandered,
but because Your mercy stayed;
Jesus, You kept me turning,
till I stand before You saved.
New every morning, Your mercies never end.
New every morning — turn me home again.
In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
